metadata.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.
metadata.content: US Open chief Craig Tiley tells Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping day and night format at Flushing Meadows in 2027 | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive US Open chief Craig Tiley tells Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping day and night format at Flushing Meadows in 2027 US Open chief Craig Tiley vows to keep same day and night format despite Ben Shelton beating Carlos Alcaraz at 3:33am local time; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Thursday 10 September 2026 22:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player US Open chief Craig Tiley backs day and night sessions despite 3am finishes US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027. Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule. It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages. The Springboks, from 1-0 down, seek to win the series 3-1 on Saturday at the home of the NFL's Baltimore Ravens, while the All Blacks are hoping to square the first traditional series between them in 30 years. South Africa scored one try in the first Test which they lost, three tries in the second Test which they won, and four in last weekend's third Test where they were at their most expansive yet. Joe Root's susceptibility to lbw and England's failure to convert starts into centuries are the only blots on an improved post-Bazball batting display, according to Nasser Hussain. England piled on 453 runs to establish a commanding first-innings lead of 320 in the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston. The hosts were firmly in control and on course for a 3-0 series sweep, with Pakistan closing on 52-2, still 268 runs adrift, when rain curtailed play. messages.text: Joshua's driver in fatal car crash has trial adjourned

metadata.summary: The trial of Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, the driver involved in the crash that injured boxer Anthony Joshua and killed two members of his team, has been adjourned until November 17.
metadata.content: Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17 | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17 Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode was driving an SUV that struck a stationary truck on December 29 2025, injuring Anthony Joshua and killing two members of his team; He is facing a four-count charge Thursday 10 September 2026 18:47, UK Image: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode (right) pictured arriving at court in January The trial of Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, the driver involved in the crash that injured boxer Anthony Joshua and killed two members of his team, has been adjourned until November 17. The case, which began in January at a magistrate court in Ogun State, was adjourned from September 10 as proceedings continued over charges arising from the fatal crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach, Sina Ghami, were killed. Kayode faces charges including dangerous driving causing death, reckless and negligent driving, driving without due care and attention, and operating a vehicle without a valid national driver's licence. The 46-year-old Kayode denies the charges. Prosecutors allege that Kayode was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the SUV carrying Joshua and his team crashed into a stationary truck.
